issues.body: `definition_time_parts` scans every `type_params` node, but PEP 695 type-parameter bounds and constraints are lazily evaluated in Python 3.12, when the bound or constraints attribute is accessed, rather than while the function or class is defined. Thus a definition such as `def f[T: _load_module(Path(__file__).resolve().with_name("lazy.py"), "x")](): ...` is reported as an import-time sibling even though importing the module does not execute that load. This violates the function's import-time-only contract and makes the LIVE declared-vs-derived exactness check demand a phantom checkout dependency. There is also no fixture exercising this newly added `type_params` branch.
issues.fix_hint: Do not scan lazy PEP 695 bound/constraint/default expressions as definition-time parts. Model their actual runtime evaluation semantics for each supported Python version, and add a Python-3.12-capable synthetic fixture proving a loader in a type-parameter bound is excluded while genuinely eager decorators/defaults remain included.
issues.title: Lazy PEP 695 type-parameter bounds are misclassified as import-time loads

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-2 defect is fixed for decorators, defaults, keyword-only defaults, lambdas, methods, and runtime-evaluated annotations, with non-vacuous boundary fixtures. However, the new PEP 695 handling classifies type-parameter expressions as definition-time execution. On Python 3.12 those bounds and constraints are lazily evaluated, so this can derive a checkout dependency that is not required at module import and contradicts the exactness contract. This is a new major finding, so progress is regressing under the required scale.
